holidays.name: National Sandwich Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to everything stacked between two slices of bread, from humble PB&J to towering deli monsters. Sandwich lovers everywhere are encouraged to build, eat, and brag about their creations.
holidays.origin: Observed in the United States as an unofficial food holiday, it is widely celebrated on November 3, which is also the birthday of John Montagu, 4th Earl of Sandwich, born in 1718, the man the sandwich is traditionally named after.
holidays.funFact: Legend says the Earl asked for meat tucked between bread so he could keep playing cards without greasy fingers, though some historians think he may have actually been working at his desk.

holidays.name: Cliché Day
holidays.description: A day to embrace every worn-out phrase in the book. Avoiding clichés like the plague is off the table, because at the end of the day, it is what it is.
holidays.origin: This unofficial observance started as a lighthearted way to poke fun at overused expressions in writing and speech, and it has been passed around among word lovers and bloggers.
holidays.funFact: The word cliché comes from a French printing term for a stereotype plate, whose metal casting made the same phrase easy to reproduce over and over.

holidays.name: Housewife's Day
holidays.description: Also known as a day to recognize those who keep the household running, it invites people to say thanks to the folks who manage home life, often with a little pampering and a break from chores.
holidays.origin: The unofficial observance is traditionally marked on November 3 in the United States, started to honor the unpaid labor and effort that goes into managing a home.
holidays.funFact: Household management used to be considered a full-time profession, and 19th-century guides like Mrs. Beeton's Book of Household Management sold in huge numbers as a kind of CEO handbook for the home.

holidays.name: Culture Day (Bunka no Hi)
holidays.description: A Japanese national holiday celebrating culture, the arts, and academic endeavor, with festivals, exhibitions, and award ceremonies popping up across the country.
holidays.origin: Established in 1948 to promote peace, freedom, and culture after World War II. The date was chosen because it was the birthday of Emperor Meiji, and also marks the day the postwar constitution was promulgated in 1946.
holidays.funFact: Each Culture Day, Japan's Order of Culture is awarded by the Emperor to people who have made outstanding contributions to arts, science, and culture.

holidays.name: Stress Awareness Day
holidays.description: A day to take a breath, put down your to-do list, and acknowledge just how stressed everyone is, with plenty of encouragement to meditate, stretch, or nap.
holidays.origin: International Stress Awareness Day was launched by the International Stress Management Association (ISMA UK) in 1998 and is held on the first Wednesday of November, which in some years falls on November 3.
holidays.funFact: The word stress was borrowed from physics by endocrinologist Hans Selye in the 1930s, and he is often called the father of stress research.
